subject: general
question: If the radius of a sphere is increased to twelve times its original radius, then by how many times does its surface area increase?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface area of a **sphere** is proportional to the **square of its radius** (Area ∝ r²).

Ratio of **Radii** = 1 : 12

Ratio of **Surface Areas** = 1² : 12² = 1 : 144

The surface area becomes **144 times** its original value.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial radius = r, New radius (R) = 12r

**Formula Used:** Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1f643f0abd9e5ca1e9fbcb533c14fdb6ed4c4ea8be1365c5d6900cdcbc90288.png] 

⇒ Initial Surface Area (A₁) = 4πr²

⇒ New Surface Area (A₂) = 4π(12r)²

⇒ A₂ = 4π × 144r²

⇒ A₂ = 144 × (4πr²)

⇒ A₂ = 144 × A₁

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by V = (4/3)πr³. If the radius is increased **n times**, the volume increases by **n³ times**.

Hemisphere Calculations

For a **hemisphere**, the Curved Surface Area is 2πr² and the Total Surface Area is 3πr².

Ratio of Areas vs Radii

In any **3D shape**, the ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of their **corresponding linear dimensions** (side, radius, or height).</p
